name: torso v1
note: torso v1 (2026-10-13), for torso_v1_post.py / torso_v1_field.py, appended after P-pelvis2. Anatomy review 2026-10-13 finding 1 (Nick, 2026-10-13: "Yes, fix all ten of them."): the trunk read as a flat board in front and a hump plus a deep hollow behind. Stage 1 is a depth-only warp (vertices move along y only, so every front-view width, body B, is unchanged): the measured midline profiles (profile: a fit of y = a + b x^2 + c dz to the vertices within fitX of the midline, per z) are taken to the target profiles (front: chest forward about .012 at z .16 to .20, a slight belly round below, back to the old line by z -.10; back: upper-back hump lowered about .01 at z .26 to .28, lumbar hollow filled about .04 at z .08, the rise into the rump eased above the tail attachment), natural cubic splines through the targets, the change smoothed along z (deltaSmooth), faded outside zBand, spread round the section by a smootherstep ramp from the side (split, rampSmooth), faded toward the arms (xIn, xOut), nothing behind y .08 (yCut: the tails and their root). Stage 2: a masked Gaussian blur (sigma .025) of the warped skin signed distance over the lumbar back, wide enough to reach the back corners but not the sides (grid; blurs), vertices moved onto it (project, relax, untangle as hips v1), which takes out the rest of the old lumbar crease where it bends across the back. World units, +y back. region: the only vertices the step may move.
